concerns.text: The plan proposes computing Pearson and Spearman correlations between the numeric `window size` (values 0, 64, 32, 16, 1) and mIoU. Since `window size` is a categorical treatment of attention sparsity (with 0 representing global attention, which is not on the same numeric scale as patch counts), treating it as a continuous numeric predictor can produce misleading correlation coefficients. A more appropriate approach would be to treat sparsity levels as an ordered factor and use non‑parametric trend tests (e.g., Jonckheere‑Terpstra) or to model the relationship with a mixed‑effects regression that respects the categorical nature of the predictor.
